issue.description:
## Scope
Re-run leg (a) of the parent stranger test — the one-line-installer binary — as ONE script, and paste the full output on this bead. Attempt 2 (2026-10-26) already ran this leg clean and pasted it in the parent notes; this child produces fresh per-child evidence the parent close can cite. Evidence-only: make NO repository file changes.

## CRITICAL — base directory trap
Do NOT use the parent acceptance template base (mktemp -d ~/scratch/...) verbatim: ~/scratch symlinks into /data/build/scratch, which contains a STRAY .beads store. Workspace discovery walks ancestors, adopts it ("Workspace already exists at: /data/build/scratch"), and the run silently exercises junk beads instead of a fresh workspace — it still exits 0, so it looks green while proving nothing. Attempt 2 hit exactly this. Use a base with no .beads in any ancestor: verify /data/build, /data and / contain no .beads (they were clean on 2026-10-26), then d=$(mktemp -d /data/build/stranger-clean-inst.XXXXXX).

## Script (ONE script, clean PATH head, no host bead env)
```bash
set -euo pipefail
d=$(mktemp -d /data/build/stranger-clean-inst.XXXXXX)
trap 'rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then rm -rf "$d"; else echo "kept $d for diagnosis" >&2; fi' EXIT
env -u BEAD_ORG_SECRET_SCANNER BEAD_INSTALL_PATH="$d/bin/bead" PATH="$d/bin:$PATH" bash -euo pipefail -c '
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/bead-rs/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
  test "$(command -v bead)" = "'"$d"'/bin/bead" && bead --version
  mkdir -p "'"$d"'/ws" && cd "'"$d"'/ws" && git init -q
  # ONLY the README Quick start, copied verbatim (including --fencing-token 1 on close)
'
```

## Acceptance (paste the full output on this bead)
- Installer exits 0; checksum verified; bead --version prints the release version (0.2.6 as of 2026-10-26).
- Quick start run verbatim from README.md on current main; output pasted.
- Lifecycle shape confirmed: the first list --ready shows design and docs (store still blocked by the blocks edge); after close, store has joined the frontier.
- Fresh-workspace proof in the pasted output: init prints Root: <your $d>/ws with a NEW UUID — not "Workspace already exists".
- Known harmless noise, not failures: "Structured diagnostics written to: .../pluck-diagnostics.json" lines (a host diagnostics setting leaking in).
- If any Quick start command fails on the released binary, record exactly which command, its exit code and stderr; do NOT edit the README here (the next child reconciles) and do NOT cut a release.
- Zero repository changes; close this bead with the pasted transcript as evidence.
